issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for Person.birthday across artifacts: the problem statement and the template Common model define Person.birthday as java.time.LocalDate, but the solution's Common Person model uses String. This cross-artifact inconsistency will confuse students about the expected data type, serialization, and UI interactions (DatePicker uses LocalDate). It may also lead to incompatible implementations or test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person.birthday type consistent across all artifacts. Prefer restoring java.time.LocalDate (as stated in the problem) in the solution's Common Person class and update any related code (serialization/deserialization and UI conversions). Alternatively, if String is intentional, update the problem statement, template model, and UI code to use String and document the expected format.

issues.description: Internal inconsistency inside the solution repository: PersonScene treats a person's birthday as a LocalDate (used with DatePicker.setValue), but the solution's Common Person model defines birthday as a String. This mismatch will cause compilation errors and blocks students trying to run or inspect the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the types consistent within the solution. Change the solution's Common Person.birthday to java.time.LocalDate (and adjust getter/setter types), or else adapt PersonScene to convert between String and LocalDate explicitly. The cleaner fix is to use LocalDate in the model and ensure JSON (de)serialization and UI usage align.
